judge_assessment.explanation: Every cited value checks out against worksheet.tex and verify.json, item by item. Problem 3's table is 'Tickets 4 | 8 | 1' over 'Cost 52 | (blank) | (blank)' -- two printed cells, and verify.json id 3 is a single eval 52/4 -> 13, so the 8-ticket cell (104) has no check. Problem 4 is 'Hours 3 | 2 | 1' over 'Miles 156 | (blank) | (blank)'; id 4 is a single eval 156/3 -> 52, so the 2-hour cell (also 104) is uncovered -- the judge's 'including 104 in problems 3 and 4' is literally correct, both cells happen to be 104. Problem 5's table has a 'Dollars per pound' column with a blank on BOTH rows plus 'decide which store is cheaper'; id 5 is one approx 28/8 -> 3.5, so Store A's 20/5 = 4 and the store selection are unchecked. Problem 6's table is 'Cups 3 | 1 | 7'; id 6 is one solve 3x - 12*7 -> [28], so the per-cup cell (4) is unchecked. Problem 8's table is 'Boxes 6 | 1 | 4'; id 8 is one eval 138/6 -> 23, so the 4-box cell (92) is unchecked. Problem 9's table is 'Minutes 12 | 1 | (blank)' over 'Gallons 84 | (blank) | 210'; id 9 is one solve -> [30], so the 7-gallons-per-minute cell is unchecked. The second hard failure is equally exact: problem 7 ends 'say in one sentence what it tells you about who is faster' and problem 10 opens 'Explain in one sentence why that reasoning is not enough', while verify.json declares eval entries only and final_response.md states '10 of 10 machine-verified, 0 manual'. The judge's mathematics is confirmed independently: 3, 15, 13/104, 52/104, 4 and 3.5 with B cheaper, 4 and 28, 3 and 3 with difference 0, 23 and 92, 7 and 30, 6 and 5 with the large pack better. Ten problems on five pages, nothing clipped.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 7 is the best-designed item on the sheet: Maya's 12 laps in 4 minutes and Dev's 21 laps in 7 minutes are both exactly 3 laps per minute, so the difference is 0. It is the only construction that makes 'more laps means faster' fail loudly instead of quietly, and the key names that explicitly ('Comparing lap totals alone would have said Dev was faster by 9 laps, which is the trap this problem is built on').

The concept-models requirement is met structurally rather than decoratively: every one of the ten problems carries its own ratio table with an explicit '1' column heading, and the directions box ties the model to the notation in one instruction -- 'Fill in the "per one" column first --- that column is the unit rate. Write the division you used beside the table.' The model and the symbol appear in the same visual object.

Nine of the ten problems declare an answer_unit that is bound in both directions -- \answerline{dollars per bar}, {pages per minute}, {miles per hour}, {crayons per box}, {minutes}, {muffins}, {dollars per pound}, {dollars per bottle} -- so the unit the student must write is gated, not merely suggested. For a unit-rate sheet the unit IS half the answer.

The comparison problems escalate honestly: problem 5 compares two straightforward rates, problem 7 makes the rates equal, and problem 10 embeds a named student's wrong reasoning to be refuted. Three different demands on the same facet with no shared skeleton.

root_causes.description: The verify entry is authored for the problem's ANSWER LINE, not for the printed table. Nine table cells the student must fill (104, 104, Store A's 4, 4 muffins per cup, 92, 7 gallons per minute, Maya's 3, Dev's 3, and the small pack's 6) are left blank on the worksheet, are printed as finished numbers in the answer key, and appear nowhere in verify.json. They are therefore hand transcriptions with no gate between the key and the check -- exactly the class of number the verifier exists to eliminate.
evidence: worksheet.tex lines 50-51 (Tickets 4|8|1 over Cost 52|blank|blank) vs verify.json id 3 = one eval -> 13
worksheet.tex lines 62-63 (Hours 3|2|1 over Miles 156|blank|blank) vs verify.json id 4 = one eval -> 52
worksheet.tex lines 76-78 (Store A/B with a blank 'Dollars per pound' cell each) vs verify.json id 5 = one approx -> 3.5
worksheet.tex lines 116-117 (Boxes 6|1|4 over Crayons 138|blank|blank) vs verify.json id 8 = one eval -> 23
answer_key.pdf problem 8 prints '23 x 4 = 92 crayons' -- the 92 exists only as key prose

root_causes.description: Two problems demand a written sentence and neither is declared manual, so the sheet reports 0 manual items. Worse, the delivery text shows the author system NOTICED the gap and reasoned it away: final_response.md ends by dismissing 'the story quantities the check does not itself divide (e.g. Store A's 5 pounds, whose rate the student computes but the JSON entry checks Store B's)' as 'the expected false-flag class the checker documents'. The prose gate had actually flagged the right thing and the rationalisation suppressed it.
evidence: worksheet problem 7: 'say in one sentence what it tells you about who is faster'
worksheet problem 10: 'Explain in one sentence why that reasoning is not enough'
final_response.md: 'both are the expected false-flag class the checker documents'

root_causes.description: Problem 7's declared trap never reaches the grader. render_quick_answers.common_errors() skips any trap where `value` is None, and verify.py's validate_traps treats `value` as optional ('if "value" in t'), so a trap can be fully machine-checked as distinguishable yet silently vanish from the key's 'Common wrong answers' block. Here the block prints only problems 5 and 10 while final_response.md claims '3 traps declared ... They print in the key's "common wrong answers" block.'
evidence: verify.json id 7 trap: {"desc": "compared the lap totals instead of the laps-per-minute rates", "expr": "a - c"} -- no "value" key
answer_key.pdf 'Common wrong answers' lists only '5. If they got 0.29' and '10. If they got 18'
scripts/render_quick_answers.py common_errors(): 'if desc is None or val is None: continue'
scripts/verify.py validate_traps(): value is guarded by 'if "value" in t', i.e. optional
final_response.md: '3 traps declared, all confirmed distinguishable ... They print in the key's "common wrong answers" block.'

improvements.title: Every blank table cell on the worksheet needs its own verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat a blank cell in a printed \begin{tabular} as a response slot. Add a gate that counts empty cells in each problem's tabular environments (cells whose body is empty or whitespace before the \\ or &) and fails when a problem's blank-cell count exceeds its verify-entry count. On this sheet the fix is nine added entries: id 3 eval 52*8/4 -> 104; id 4 eval 156*2/3 -> 104; id 5 eval 20/5 -> 4 plus a choice entry for Store B; id 6 eval 12/3 -> 4; id 7 eval 12/4 -> 3 and eval 21/7 -> 3; id 8 eval 138*4/6 -> 92; id 9 eval 84/12 -> 7; id 10 eval 18/3 -> 6. Every one of those numbers is already printed in the answer key, so the entries record what the key already asserts instead of leaving it as untested prose.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a tabular 'Tickets 4 | 8 | 1' over 'Cost 52 | & | &' (two blank cells) and a verify JSON with one eval entry for that id. Assert the build fails naming the id and the blank-cell/entry counts (2 vs 1). Today curr-156's identical shape passes all 21 gates.
improvements.expected_impact: Raises this sheet's coverage from 10 checks over 22 printed slots to full coverage, and closes the judge's first hard failure. Because the missing numbers are already typed into the answer key, the change also converts nine untested key assertions into gated ones.
improvements.risk: Medium. Blank cells that are deliberately decorative (spacer columns, a header row's leading corner) would false-fail. Mitigate by only counting cells inside a tabular that also contains at least one \answerline-bearing problem, and by allowing an explicit per-problem 'blank_cells' override in the JSON for the rare decorative case.

improvements.title: The two 'explain in one sentence' items must be declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a `manual` entry under id 7 ('Says the two rates are equal, so neither runner is faster -- not "Dev is faster because he ran more laps"') and under id 10 ('Says comparing 18 to 25 compares totals for different numbers of bottles, so it cannot decide value'). Both sentences already exist verbatim in the answer key's solutions. Systemically, make the build refuse to emit a delivery claim of '0 manual' when any stem contains 'explain', 'say in one sentence', 'why', 'describe' or 'justify'; the check belongs in the same lint that scans stems, and the honest outcome is exit 2 with the ids listed.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem contains 'Explain in one sentence why that reasoning is not enough' with a verify JSON holding only an eval entry for id 1. Assert exit 2 with id 1 reported as manual. Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text is free to print '0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Manual count goes 0 -> 2, gate_chain_manual_flags flips true, and the judge's second hard failure disappears. It also removes the specific dishonesty the delivery text committed here, where a known gap was labelled an expected false flag.
improvements.risk: Medium: prose verb matching will over-flag stems that use 'why' inside a hint. Ship as exit-2 visibility rather than a build failure so a correct sheet is never blocked.

improvements.title: A declared trap with no `value` is machine-checked but never printed for the grader
improvements.proposed_change: Make `value` required whenever a trap is declared, or compute it. verify.py's check_traps already evaluates the trap expr to a concrete number (`tv`) in order to prove the problem's comparison rejects it; emit that computed value into the verify report and have render_quick_answers.common_errors() use it instead of skipping the row. Either way, delete the silent `continue` in common_errors() -- a trap that cannot be rendered should fail the build, not disappear.
improvements.regression_test: Render a verify JSON containing {"id": 7, "type": "eval", "expr": "a/b - c/d", "at": {"a": 12, "b": 4, "c": 21, "d": 7}, "expected": 0, "traps": [{"desc": "compared the lap totals", "expr": "a - c"}]} and assert the 'Common wrong answers' block contains a row for problem 7 with the value -9. Fails today: the row is dropped and the block shows only the traps that happened to carry a hand-typed `value`.
improvements.expected_impact: Problem 7's trap -- the single most instructive misconception on this sheet, since it is the reason the problem was built -- reaches the grader. It also makes the delivery text's claim that all declared traps print become true rather than aspirational.
improvements.risk: Low. Making `value` derived rather than hand-typed strictly increases trust; the only behavioural change is that a previously silent skip becomes either a printed row or a loud failure.

case_summary: A genuinely good concept-models sheet: every problem carries its own ratio table with an explicit 'per one' column so the model and the notation share one object, nine problems bind an answer unit in both directions, and the three comparison items escalate from two plain rates (problem 5) to two EQUAL rates (problem 7, both runners at 3 laps per minute, so the difference is 0 and 'more laps means faster' fails loudly) to refuting a named student's reasoning (problem 10). All the mathematics recomputes correctly. It is rejected because verification covers one scalar per problem while the sheet prints twenty-two response slots. Nine blank table cells -- 104 in problem 3, 104 in problem 4, Store A's 4 dollars per pound, 4 muffins per cup, 92 crayons, 7 gallons per minute, both runners' 3 laps per minute, and the small pack's 6 dollars per bottle -- appear as finished numbers in the answer key and nowhere in verify.json, so they are untested transcriptions. Problems 7 and 10 each demand a written sentence and neither is declared manual. Two findings beyond the judge: the delivery text shows the gap was noticed and rationalised away as 'the expected false-flag class the checker documents', and problem 7's declared trap carries no `value` field, so render_quick_answers.common_errors() silently drops it and the key prints only two of the three traps the delivery text says are printed.
